claims: NPD is the published dataset of HM Land Registry index polygons for England and Wales.
A registered title normally has a title plan, a register and one or more index polygons.
title plan and register record the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary is determined.
an index polygon provides an index showing the indicative location of a registered title.
index polygons are held in vector format.
title plan and register share the title number identifier.
every registered title has at least one index polygon.
each index polygon has a unique Poly_ID.
title number manages the relationship between a registered title and its polygons.
index polygons are mapped against OS large-scale MasterMap data.
polygons may follow mapped features where those features relate to ownership boundaries.
ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in MasterMap.
NPD is a subset of the Land Register containing registered titles relating to land or property.
NPD links to Title Descriptor and UPRN datasets through title number.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of NPD with simpler attributes.
NPD mandatory fields include Shape, Poly_ID, Title_No, INSERT, UPDATE, Vers_No and Rec_Status.
Shape must be a single-area geometry.
INSERT records initial creation date on the index map.
UPDATE records the date all or part of the title was last updated.
Vers_No records the version of Poly_ID.
Rec_Status uses Added, Changed and Deleted states.
overlaps, gaps, slivers and underlaps exist in NPD.
technical overlaps can arise from mapping inconsistencies and need not represent real title conflict.
actual overlaps may represent two or more titles including the same land or property.
acceptable overlaps can arise from floor levels, strata, tenures and title classes.
minor overlaps below 0.5 square metres are not referred for remedial action.
some gaps or underlaps are legitimate because registered titles need not adjoin.
HMLR does not guarantee the public data is error-free or fit for every purpose.
an index polygon may be the same size, larger or smaller than the extent on the title plan.
index polygons must not be relied on to show the exact registered extent.
historic capture and vectorisation practices introduced inconsistencies.
some polygons were moved in sympathy with OS positional accuracy changes.
Quality Improvement Flowline reconciled many polygons with title plans but does not make them exact boundaries.
HMLR receives daily OS MasterMap change-only updates for new work rather than routine review of all existing registrations.
all HMLR index polygon data is captured to British National Grid.
Indicative Extent is the most common feature type.
Footprint and Artificial Footprint types can intentionally exceed the title extent.
Exaggerated Extent can widen narrow registered strips for index visibility.
Gridding can split one real-world feature into polygons with separate polygon IDs at historic sheet joins.
HMLR does not routinely update title plans or index polygons.
index polygons are updated when title activity, adjoining-title work, queries or discovered errors require it.
overnight publication applies validation for zero coordinates, zero area and duplicate coordinates.
publication cleaning removes many self-intersections and polygons below 0.1 square metres.
a polygon can change several times but a COU contains only the latest version.
HMLR does not retain previous polygon versions in the COU delivery.
NPD is published and updated monthly.
files are available from the second working day of each month.
delivery includes full, change-only update and validation files.
full polygon delivery can be split into files with a 2GB limit.
candidate binding requires current polygon bytes, Poly_ID, title linkage and lifecycle status; title number alone is insufficient.
